subject: MSA & Order Form — Confidentiality, Press Notices and Logo/Reference Rights
messages:
From: Lucas Byrne <lbyrne@novacorp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ava.reynolds@marketingpartner.io
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines (confidentiality & publicity sections)

Hi Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form. Attached are NovaCorp's redlines focused on Sections 6 (Confidentiality) and 12 (Publicity/Reference Rights). Two quick flags:

- We need a tighter confidentiality carveout around benchmarking/aggregated metrics — we want aggregated usage stats excluded from marketing unless explicitly approved.
- For publicity: we cannot grant unlimited logo use. We propose an opt-in marketing clause: Redwood may request publicity/press releases and logo use, and NovaCorp will not unreasonably withhold consent but requires review within 7 business days and final approval on any quote or logo.

I've attached the marked-up doc (NVC_MSA_redlines_20260915.docx). Ava from our comms team is copied for any practical questions about logo assets/size/lockups.

Can your team confirm whether the approval window and the requested carveouts are acceptable?

Best,
Lucas Byrne
Senior Counsel, NovaCorp
[Attachment: NVC_MSA_redlines_20260915.docx]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Lucas Byrne <lbyrne@novacorp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com, ava.reynolds@marketingpartner.io
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines (confidentiality & publicity sections)

Lucas — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Looping in Ben (sales lead) and Marissa (AM/PR ops) and Sofia from Legal Ops to coordinate.

Quick responses:
- Approval window: 7 business days is a bit tight for cross-functional sign-off on some customers, but acceptable as a standard SLA if we add an automatic escalation to execs after 10 business days. Would NovaCorp accept an escalation path instead of extending the SLA?
- Benchmarking/aggregated metrics: we usually include an explicit carve-in for aggregated, anonymized usage statistics for our marketing and product benchmarking. We can add language that only non-identifying, aggregated metrics are allowed and any customer-identifying data requires explicit approval.

Sofia — can you propose concrete language we can send back that addresses both items but remains acceptable to legal?

Thanks all — goal is to get to a consolidated redline by end of week so we can move to order form sign-off.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Lucas Byrne <lbyrne@novacorp.com>, ava.reynolds@marketingpartner.io
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines (confidentiality & publicity sections)

Laura/Ben/Marissa — draft language below that I recommend we propose back to NovaCorp. I focused on keeping an operational approval window while protecting their opt-in on logo use and preserving Redwood's need for non-identifying telemetry.

Proposed substitutions (replace in MSA):

1) Confidentiality — metrics carveout: 
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Parties agree that Redwood may, without prior Customer approval, use aggregated and anonymized usage metrics derived from Customer’s use of the Services for internal product development and for inclusion in anonymized benchmarking reports or case-count style marketing materials, provided such metrics cannot reasonably be used to identify Customer or any individual. Any use of Customer-specific metrics or performance benchmarks that could reasonably be traced to Customer requires Customer’s prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed."

2) Publicity/Logo/Reference rights: 
"Customer may grant or withhold approval for any publicity, press release, testimonial, or logo use. Should Customer choose to grant approval, Customer will review and respond to Redwood’s written request within seven (7) business days. If Customer does not respond within ten (10) business days, Redwood may escalate the request to the Customer’s designated executive sponsor for a decision. Redwood will not use Customer logos other than as expressly approved and will follow Customer-provided brand guidelines. Any quote attributed to Customer will require prior written approval. Customer’s consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed."

Notes/asks: 
- Ben: confirm the escalation path is acceptable commercially; we can move to a 10 business day auto-escalate to execs.
- Marissa: once we have NovaCorp approval, we need their logo assets and brand guide (Ava — can you share the required formats).
- Lucas/Ava: if that language works, we can consolidate and send a clean MSA with tracked changes removed.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivánova
Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Sofia/Laura — thanks for the quick turn. The proposed language looks reasonable from our side. A few small edits:

- In the confidentiality carveout, change "not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed" to "not to be unreasonably withheld" (drop the delay language).
- For escalation: NovaCorp will accept the 10 business day auto-escalation to the designated executive sponsor, but we request that the MSA include the executive sponsor contact by name/email in the order form to make that operational.

Ava adds: we can provide logo assets and brand guidelines once the MSA language is finalized. We prefer raster plus SVG variants and a small style guide.

If you can incorporate the minor edit and add a placeholder in the order form for the exec sponsor, we can aim to return final sign-off by next Tuesday.

Regards,
Lucas Byrne
Senior Counsel, NovaCorp
